sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-myc immunofluorescence on non-permeabilized cells (GPMVs and intact cells); trafficking to plasma membrane unaffected; folding and function explicitly reported as non-perturbed across at least five independent studies (PMC13382790, PMC7322011, PMC9860121, PMC3110552, PMC3563111).
sites.rationale: L1 and L2 both name the junction explicitly as 'between residues 125 and 126' in full-length human PMP22; Python confirms seq[124]='H' and seq[125]='L', matching the reported letters. Position 125 sits 9 residues from the TM3 C-terminal boundary (116) and 8 residues from the TM4 N-terminal boundary (134), well within ECL2 (117–133) and clear of TM helices. No cysteines, N-glycosylation sequons, or known functional residues are present in ECL2, and the insert has been validated across multiple cell types and expression systems. Full-length human PMP22 in lentiviral (pCW57.1) and pCDNA3.1/pIRES2 expression vectors; 10-residue myc tag (EQKLISEEDL) inserted between residues 125 and 126 in the second extracellular loop (ECL2, topology residues 117–133); expressed in HEK293T, HeLa, HEC-1A, and Schwann-cell-derived lines. Anti-myc antibody labeling of non-permeabilized cells confirms surface display; multiple independent groups report no effect on folding, ER exit, plasma-membrane trafficking, or function. [validation: surface_and_function; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: The 10-residue myc tag was inserted between residues 125 and 126 in the second extracellular loop of PMP22, as this internal tag was previously demonstrated to be non-perturbative of PMP22 folding and trafficking ( Fig. 1 A ) ( 36 , 37 ).

literature_notes: L3/L4 (HA tag, mouse PMP22 ECL2), L5/L20 (Myc tag, human N41Q), L6–L14/L18/L19 (Myc tag, ECL2, various labs) all corroborate the same ECL2 insertion but name no independent residue; they reinforce L1/L2 rather than defining a second site. L15/L16 (ALFA tag) and L17 (GFP) report C-terminal fusions: the authoritative topology places residues 157–160 in the intracellular compartment, so these tags are not extracellular and are excluded. The N-terminus (residues 1–4) is likewise intracellular. No ledger line supports an ECL1 insertion with a named residue, so no ECL1 site is proposed.
